page: Vultr vbm-8c-132gb-v2 is a bare metal server configured with an Intel Xeon 2388G processor built on the x86_64 architecture. This dedicated CPU features 8 physical cores and 16 virtual cores (vCPUs) operating at a base clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled and consists of a 3840 GB NVMe SSD, while the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this hardware configuration.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression scoring in the top 25%. Multi-core CPU performance and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression fall within the average tier. Memory performance presents a tradeoff: while the Passmark memory score ranks in the top 10%, large-block uncached read and write memory bandwidth benchmarks are positioned in the bottom 25%. Database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput all perform at average levels.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this bare metal configuration offers high resource density by combining dedicated CPU cores with a substantial 128 GB memory footprint and a large 3.8 TB local NVMe SSD, avoiding the virtualization overhead of standard cloud instances. The server is well-suited for workloads requiring dedicated hardware, such as relational databases, memory-intensive caching layers, static web serving, and moderate-scale data processing tasks.
